It acts as a silica cement sourced internally from hybrid lithologies or externally from basement and arkosic units, and it can strongly modify reservoir quality by occluding or locally preserving pore space during replacement and fracture-related diagenesis.

Microquartz is a diagenetic silica phase that consists of quartz crystals smaller than 20 μm and commonly fills inter-aggregate, interparticle, and vugular pores or replaces carbonate fabric in pre-salt carbonates. In the Santos Basin pre-salt, it is the most frequent silica phase associated with pervasive silicification and is generally interpreted as a late eogenetic cement, commonly occurring with chalcedony and megaquartz.

Silica cement is a diagenetic cement that precipitates as silica minerals, mainly chalcedony and micro- to macrocrystalline quartz, lining and filling interparticle pores, vugs, and fractures in Pre-Salt carbonate reservoirs. In the Brazilian Pre-Salt, it commonly occurs as pore-lining fringes or later pore-filling/drusy quartz, locally after earlier replacement phases, and may either partly preserve excess permeability or occlude pore space depending on its timing and abundance.
Phyllosilicate Mineral is a mineral that has a sheet-silicate crystal structure.

Clay mineral is a fine-grained phyllosilicate mineral that constitutes the mud fraction of Brazilian Pre-Salt lacustrine carbonates and is commonly dominated by Mg-rich species such as kerolite, mixed-layer kerolite/Mg-smectite, Mg-smectite, and sepiolite. In the Barra Velha and related Aptian reservoirs, these minerals occur dispersed between siliciclastic grains or in very thin laminae, with minor illite, illite-smectite, kaolinite, and chlorite also present.

Stevensite is an aluminum-poor Ca-Mg smectitic clay mineral that precipitates from highly alkaline lacustrine waters, typically at pH greater than about 9, in pre-salt sag deposits. In Brazilian Pre-Salt carbonate systems, it commonly forms laminated clay-rich facies and may occur with calcitic spherulites or dolomite rhombs in low-energy, relatively deeper lake settings. It is commonly compacted and later partially dissolved or replaced by calcite or dolomite during diagenesis.

Kerolite is a magnesium-rich clay mineral that occurs as a principal authigenic Mg-clay in Aptian pre-salt lacustrine carbonate facies of the Santos Basin. In the Barra Velha reservoir succession, it is common in Mg-claystones, intraclastic grainstones, fascicular calcite crusts, and laminites, and its abundance generally increases upward into Units 2 and 1, reaching its highest proportions in Unit 1.

Talc is a magnesium-rich phyllosilicate mineral that precipitates in the Brazilian pre-salt under highly alkaline lacustrine conditions, commonly as hydrated talc formed from Mg-rich silica gel at about pH 9 to 10. In the Barra Velha Formation it is characterized by low crystallinity and a defective turbostratic structure, and its late diagenetic transformation releases silica and magnesium that favor the precipitation of silica and dolomite.

Anhydrite is an evaporite mineral that consists of anhydrous calcium sulfate and commonly forms dense, brittle basal layers of the Ariri Formation above the Barra Velha carbonates. In the Brazilian Pre-Salt, this layer marks the transition from lacustrine limestones to overlying evaporites and generates a strong positive seismic reflector because it has higher density and seismic velocity than halite, contributing to the regional sealing succession.

Halite is an evaporite mineral that consists of sodium chloride and commonly forms the dominant salt component of the Ariri Formation above the Brazilian Pre-Salt carbonates. In the Santos Basin, it is more ductile and plastic than anhydrite, so it flows during salt deformation to form thick salt bodies and diapirs. This halite-rich evaporite succession provides the regional seal over the Barra Velha reservoirs.

Mg-clay is a magnesium-rich clay mineral assemblage that forms part of the matrix of Brazilian pre-salt carbonate facies, commonly in association with calcite spherulites and dolomite. In the Santos Basin it consists mainly of Mg-smectitic clays, with rare sepiolite, and its dissolution or replacement by calcite can generate secondary porosity even though Mg-clay-rich facies are initially of low reservoir quality.

Organic matter is a sedimentary organic component that consists of preserved biological material and microbial extracellular polymeric substances incorporated into pre-salt lacustrine carbonates. In the Brazilian Pre-Salt, it commonly occurs as remnants in laminites and dark bands associated with microcrystalline calcite, dolomite, and microbial fabrics, and it may both concentrate trace elements in biofilms and later generate CO2 and organic acids during maturation.

Pyrite is an iron sulfide mineral that occurs as a common diagenetic product in Brazilian Pre-Salt rocks, forming cubic to micro- or macrocrystalline aggregates that fill fractures and veins or replace grains, matrix, and carbonate phases. In these carbonate reservoirs it is commonly associated with silica and dolomite, may develop in organic- and clay-rich rocks through thermochemical sulfate reduction, and fracture-filling pyrite can indicate remobilization during diagenesis.
A role that is borne by a facies with pore-system architecture and petrophysical properties favorable for hydrocarbon storage and flow.
A role that is borne by a subsurface body of rock that contains and transmits accumulated hydrocarbons because it has sufficient porosity, permeability, and trapping conditions.
A role that is borne by a body of rock that prevents or strongly retards the migration of hydrocarbons or other subsurface fluids, allowing their accumulation in a reservoir.
A role that is borne by a basin-scale body of rock that laterally extends over reservoir rocks and prevents upward migration and leakage of hydrocarbons.
A disposition that is borne by a body of rock and is realized when the rock stores and transmits groundwater through permeable or fractured rock.
A disposition that is borne by a sedimentary rock containing sufficient organic matter and realized in hydrocarbon generation during burial and thermal maturation.
A disposition that is borne by a sedimentary rock with sufficient porosity and permeability to store hydrocarbons and allow their flow through a subsurface reservoir.
